title: ScrapMem: A Bio-Inspired Framework for On-Device Personalized Agent Memory via Optical Forgetting
abstract: arXiv:2605.03804v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Long-term personalized memory for LLM agents is challenging on resource-limited edge devices because multimodal histories grow continually and are costly to store. To address this challenge, we propose ScrapMem, a bio-inspired framework that consolidates each day's heterogeneous records into a unified "Scrapbook Page." ScrapMem introduces Optical Forgetting, an optical compression mechanism that progressively reduces the resolution and JPEG quality of older pages, lowering storage costs while keeping recent evidence at higher fidelity. To preserve semantic consistency and support structured retrieval, we construct an Episodic Memory Graph (EM-Graph) that organizes semantic nodes into causal-temporal EM-Paths. This design separates a stable retrieval structure from aging visual evidence, allowing relevant episodes to remain accessible as page fidelity decreases. translated_title: ScrapMem：一种通过光学遗忘实现设备端个性化智能体记忆的仿生框架
translated_abstract: 长期个性化记忆对于在资源受限的边缘设备上运行的LLM智能体而言极具挑战性，因为多模态历史记录会持续增长且存储成本高昂。为应对这一挑战，我们提出了ScrapMem，一个受生物学启发的框架，它将每天的异构记录整合为统一的“剪贴簿页面”。ScrapMem引入了光学遗忘机制，这是一种光学压缩机制，通过逐步降低较旧页面的分辨率和JPEG质量来降低存储成本，同时使近期证据保持较高的保真度。为保持语义一致性并支持结构化检索，我们构建了情景记忆图，将语义节点组织成具有因果-时序结构的EM路径。这一设计将稳定的检索结构与逐渐老化的视觉证据相分离，使得即使页面保真度降低，相关情景仍然可以访问。在通用的ATM-Bench协议下，不带遗忘机制的ScrapMem确立了……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: ScrapMem提出了一种仿生的设备端智能体记忆框架，通过“光学遗忘”机制逐步压缩旧记忆页面的图像质量以降低存储成本，同时借助情景记忆图保持语义一致性与结构化检索能力。
en_tdlr: ScrapMem is a bio-inspired framework for on-device personalized agent memory that uses Optical Forgetting to progressively compress older memory pages for lower storage costs, while an Episodic Memory Graph preserves semantic consistency and structured retrieval.
